members.name: setStatus
members.doc: Sets the status.

members.name: text
members.doc:
Replaces the body with `text` and sets `Content-Type` to  
`text/plain; charset=utf-8`.

members.name: text
members.doc:
Replaces the body with `text` and sets `Content-Type` to  
`text/plain; charset=utf-8`.

members.name: write
members.doc: Appends `bytes` to the body.

members.name: writeStr
members.doc: Appends the bytes of `text` to the body.

items.name: findByte
items.signature: function findByte(text: &String, byte: u8, start: u64, end: u64): u64
items.doc:
The byte index of the first `byte` in `text` from `start` to `end`, or  
`end` when there is none.

items.name: percentDecode
items.signature: function percentDecode(text: &String, start: u64, end: u64, plusIsSpace: boolean): Option<String>
items.doc:
Decodes `%XX` escapes in the bytes of `text` from `start` to `end`, and  
`+` as a space when `plusIsSpace`. `NONE` when an escape is not two hex  
digits or the result is not UTF-8.

items.name: spells
items.signature: function spells(text: &String, start: u64, end: u64, name: str): boolean
items.doc: Whether the bytes of `text` from `start` to `end` spell `name`.

items.name: Layer
items.doc:
One registered middleware. Kept in a record rather than as a bare  
function value so that `Vector<Layer>` has a short name: the QBE backend  
spells a `Vector` of a function type out in full, and QBE rejects  
identifiers longer than 80 bytes.

members.name: handler
members.signature: handler: (&mut Request, &mut Response, (&mut Request, &mut Response) -> Result<void, Error>) -> Result<void, Error>

items.name: Route
items.doc: One registered route.

members.name: method
members.doc: The method it answers, empty for `any`.

members.name: handler
members.signature: handler: (&mut Request, &mut Response, (&mut Request, &mut Response) -> Result<void, Error>) -> Result<void, Error>

items.name: Web
items.doc: The router, the application and the server entry points.

items.name: App
items.doc:
An application: builds the router every server thread uses. It is  
shared by all threads, so it has to be `Send` and `Sync`; the routers  
it builds are not shared.

items.name: Middleware
items.signature: type Middleware = (&mut Request, &mut Response, (&mut Request, &mut Response) -> Result<void, Error>) -> Result<void, Error>
items.doc:
A middleware or a route: the request, the response and the rest of  
the chain.

items.name: Next
items.signature: type Next = (&mut Request, &mut Response) -> Result<void, Error>
items.doc:
What a middleware or route calls to run the rest of the chain. It  
returns once the rest of the chain did, with its error if it failed.

items.name: Router
items.doc:
Middleware and routes for one thread. A router holds function values,  
which are neither `Send` nor `Sync`, so it never leaves the thread  
that built it; `Web::App` builds one per server thread.

members.name: new
members.doc:
A router without middleware or routes: it answers every request  
with 404.

members.name: allowedMethods
members.doc:
The methods of the routes whose path matches `segments`, in the  
order they were added, as an `Allow` value. A `GET` route allows  
`HEAD` too.

members.name: any
members.signature: any(&mut self, path: str, handler: (&mut Request, &mut Response, (&mut Request, &mut Response) -> Result<void, Error>) -> Result<void, Error>): void
members.doc: Adds a route for requests to `path` with any method.

members.name: delete
members.signature: delete(&mut self, path: str, handler: (&mut Request, &mut Response, (&mut Request, &mut Response) -> Result<void, Error>) -> Result<void, Error>): void
members.doc: Adds a route for `DELETE` requests to `path`.

members.name: dispatch
members.signature: dispatch(&self, request: &mut Request, response: &mut Response): Result<void, Error>

members.name: get
members.signature: get(&mut self, path: str, handler: (&mut Request, &mut Response, (&mut Request, &mut Response) -> Result<void, Error>) -> Result<void, Error>): void
members.doc: Adds a route for `GET` (and `HEAD`) requests to `path`.

members.name: handle
members.doc:
Answers `request` through `dispatch`. An error that reaches the  
router becomes a response with its status and its message as a  
plain-text body; header fields already set stay.

members.name: patch
members.signature: patch(&mut self, path: str, handler: (&mut Request, &mut Response, (&mut Request, &mut Response) -> Result<void, Error>) -> Result<void, Error>): void
members.doc: Adds a route for `PATCH` requests to `path`.

members.name: post
members.signature: post(&mut self, path: str, handler: (&mut Request, &mut Response, (&mut Request, &mut Response) -> Result<void, Error>) -> Result<void, Error>): void
members.doc: Adds a route for `POST` requests to `path`.

members.name: put
members.signature: put(&mut self, path: str, handler: (&mut Request, &mut Response, (&mut Request, &mut Response) -> Result<void, Error>) -> Result<void, Error>): void
members.doc: Adds a route for `PUT` requests to `path`.

members.name: route
members.signature: route(&mut self, method: str, path: str, handler: (&mut Request, &mut Response, (&mut Request, &mut Response) -> Result<void, Error>) -> Result<void, Error>): void
members.doc:
Adds a route for `method`, written as it appears on the request  
line (`OPTIONS`, `PURGE`), or every method when it is empty.

members.name: runLayer
members.signature: runLayer(&self, index: u64, request: &mut Request, response: &mut Response): Result<void, Error>

members.name: runRoute
members.signature: runRoute(&self, start: u64, segments: &Vector<String>, request: &mut Request, response: &mut Response): Result<void, Error>
members.doc:
Runs the first route from `start` on that matches the request, with  
a `next` that continues from the route after it. When none is left,  
the request is answered with 404, or with 405 and `Allow` when no  
route matched its method but some matched its path.

members.name: use
members.signature: use(&mut self, middleware: (&mut Request, &mut Response, (&mut Request, &mut Response) -> Result<void, Error>) -> Result<void, Error>): void
members.doc:
Adds a middleware. Middleware runs for every request, matched or  
not, in the order it was added, before any route.

items.name: serve
items.signature: function serve<A>(address: &SocketAddress, config: ServerConfig, app: A): Result<void, IoError>
items.doc:
Binds `address` and serves `app` on `config.threads` threads, as  
`serveListener` does.

items.name: serveListener
items.signature: function serveListener<A>(listener: TcpListener, config: ServerConfig, app: A): Result<void, IoError>
items.doc:
Serves `app` on `listener` with `config.threads` threads (0 counts as  
1). Each thread calls `app.build()` once and serves its connections  
with that router through `Http::acceptConnections`. Returns once  
every thread stopped, with the first thread's error; like  
`Http::Server::run`, in practice it blocks for as long as the process  
lives.

items.name: __closure_thunk_0
items.signature: function __closure_thunk_0(__closure_env_0: *mut u8, innerRequest: &mut Request, innerResponse: &mut Response): Result<void, Error>

items.name: __closure_thunk_1
items.signature: function __closure_thunk_1(__closure_env_1: *mut u8, innerRequest: &mut Request, innerResponse: &mut Response): Result<void, Error>

items.name: addMethod
items.doc:
Appends `method` to `methods` unless it is already there. An empty  
method (a route for any method) is skipped: such a route matches every  
method, so it never leads to a 405.

items.name: isParameter
items.doc: Whether `segment` of a route path is a parameter, `:name`.

items.name: matchSegments
items.doc:
Matches the route `pattern` against the request `segments`. `OK(NONE)`  
when the path does not match, `OK(SOME(params))` with the decoded  
parameters when it does, and a 400 error when a parameter is not valid  
percent-encoded UTF-8.

items.name: methodMatches
items.doc:
Whether a route with `method` (empty for `any`) answers `requested`. A  
`HEAD` request is answered by `GET` routes.

items.name: pathSegments
items.doc:
The segments of a path: the parts between `/` after the leading one.  
`/` has one empty segment and `/users/` ends with one. A path that does  
not start with `/`, such as `*`, has none and matches no route.
